'''''Echium vulgare''''', known as '''viper's bugloss''' and '''blueweed''',<ref name=ROM>Dickinson, T.; Metsger, D.; Bull, J.; & Dickinson, R. (2004) ROM Field Guide to Wildflowers of Ontario. Toronto:Royal Ontario Museum, p. 203.</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[borage]] family [[Boraginaceae]]. It is [[Native species|native]] to most of [[Europe]] and western and central [[Asia]]<ref name=flora>''Flora Europaea'': [http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Echium&SPECIES_XREF=vulgare&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK= ''Echium vulgare'']</ref><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 17 December 2017}}</ref> and it occurs as an [[introduced species]] in north-eastern [[North America]], south-western South America and the South and North Island of New Zealand.<ref name=ROM/><ref>{{cite web| work=Plants of the World Online| title=Echium vulgare L.|publisher=Royal Botanic Garden, Kew|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:115950-1|access-date=18 December 2022}}</ref> If eaten, the plant is [[Toxicity|toxic]] to [[horse]]s and [[cattle]] through the accumulation of [[pyrrolizidine alkaloid]]s in the [[liver]].<ref name="GPP">{{cite web |title=Guide to Poisonous Plants – College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences |url=https://csuvth.colostate.edu/poisonous_plants/Plants/Details/38 |access-date=19 September 2020 |website=csuvth.colostate.edu |publisher=Colorado State University}}</ref><ref name="Klemow2002">{{cite journal |last1=Klemow |first1=Kenneth M. |last2=Clements |first2=David R. |last3=Threadgill |first3=Paul F. |last4=Cavers |first4=Paul B. |date=1 January 2002 |title=The biology of Canadian weeds. 116. Echium vulgare L. |journal=Canadian Journal of Plant Science |volume=82 |issue=1 |pages=235–248 |doi=10.4141/P01-058 |doi-access=}}</ref>

The plant [[root]] was used in ancient times as a treatment for [[snake]] or [[Viperidae|viper]] [[Snakebite|bites]].<ref name="MissBot">{{cite web |title=Echium vulgare - Plant Finder |url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277970 |access-date=19 September 2020 |website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Coles |first=William |title=Adam in Eden, or Nature's Paradise. The History of Plants, Herbs, Flowers, with their several, . . names, whether Greek, Latin, or English, and . . . vertues |date=1657 |location=London |pages=187}}</ref> According to the [[Doctrine of signatures]], plants were thought to have traits (in this case a speckled stem reminiscent of snake skin, and flowers like an open viper's mouth) that mirror the ailment they treat.<ref name="ScienceMus2">{{cite web |title=Doctrine of Signatures |url=http://www.sciencemuseum.org.uk/broughttolife/techniques/doctrine.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140103201719/http://www.sciencemuseum.org.uk/broughttolife/techniques/doctrine.aspx |archive-date=January 3, 2014 |access-date=February 8, 2014 |publisher=Science Museum}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-28 |title=Viper's Bugloss |url=https://congletonbhpg.co.uk/our-plants/vipers-bugloss/ |access-date=2025-06-11 |website=Congleton Bath House & Physic Garden |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Description==
It is a [[biennial plant|biennial]] or [[monocarpic]] [[perennial plant]] growing to {{convert|30|–|80|cm|abbr=on}} tall, with rough, hairy, [[Glossary of leaf morphology#Leaf and leaflet shapes|oblanceolate]] [[leaf|leaves]].<ref name="Graves">{{cite web|last1=Graves|first1=Melissa|last2=Mangold|first2=Jane|last3=Jacobs|first3=Jim|title=Biology, Ecology and Management of Blueweed|url=http://store.msuextension.org/publications/AgandNaturalResources/EB0195.pdf|website=store.msuextension.org|publisher=Montana State University|access-date=22 October 2016}}</ref> The stems, which are red-flecked, resemble snake's skin and even the fruits are shaped like adders' heads.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Echium vulgare - Viper's Bugloss |url=https://www.first-nature.com/flowers/echium-vulgare.php |access-date=2024-09-20 |website=www.first-nature.com}}</ref> The flowers start pink and turn vivid blue, and are {{convert|15|-|20|mm|abbr=on}} in a branched spike, with all the [[stamen]]s protruding. The [[pollen]] is blue<ref name="Hodges">{{cite book|author=Dorothy Hodges|title=The pollen loads of the honeybee|year=1952|publisher=Bee Research Association Ltd., London}}</ref> but the filaments of the [[stamen]]s remain red, contrasting against the blue flowers. It flowers between May and September in the [[Northern Hemisphere]]. The Latin specific epithet ''vulgare'' means common.<ref name="MissBot" />

==Distribution==
It is native to Europe and temperate Asia. It has been introduced to [[Chile]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Description and images of Echium vulgare (Hierba azul, Viborera, Ortiguilla), a native Chilean plant, provided by the supplier of native exotic Chilean seeds, Chileflora.com |url=http://www.chileflora.com/Florachilena/FloraEnglish/HighResPages/EH0022.htm |access-date=2022-11-21 |website=www.chileflora.com}}</ref> [[New Zealand]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Echium vulgare|url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/echium-vulgare/|access-date=2020-11-28|website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network|language=en}}</ref> and [[North America]], where it is [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in parts of the continent including [[Ontario]] and northern [[Michigan]],<ref name=grin/> being listed as an [[invasive species]] in [[Washington (state)|Washington]].<ref name="atlas">{{cite web|title=Common viper's bugloss: Echium vulgare (Lamiales: Boraginaceae): Invasive Plant Atlas of the United States|url=http://www.invasiveplantatlas.org/subject.html?sub=5564|website=www.invasiveplantatlas.org|publisher=Invasive Plant Atlas of the United States|access-date=22 October 2016}}</ref> It is found in dry, [[calcareous]] [[grassland]] and [[heath]]s, bare and waste places, along [[railway]]s and roadsides and on [[Cliffed coast|coastal cliffs]], [[Dune|sand dunes]] and [[Shingle beach|shingle]].<ref name=fitter>Fitter, R. & A. (1974). ''The Wild Flowers of Britain and Northern Europe''. Collins.</ref>

==Cultivation==
''E. vulgare'' is cultivated as an ornamental plant, and numerous [[cultivar]]s have been developed. The cultivar 'Blue Bedder' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web
| url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/139228/i-Echium-vulgare-i-Blue-Bedder/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Echium vulgare'' 'Blue Bedder' | access-date=12 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 35 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 24 January 2018}}</ref>
